d: We’re Building the Future of Capital Markets; enabling entrepreneurship, job creation, financial inclusion, and economic resilience

As Asia's largest licensed digital securities exchange for alternative investments, Alta is at the forefront of building critical capital market infrastructure. We believe that access to capital markets are pivotal in all economies, we recognize that our role in building this critical infrastructure goes beyond facilitating trades; it paves the way for entrepreneurship, job creation, financial inclusion, and economic resilience, fostering a brighter future for emerging markets and economies.

Empowering Private Markets: Through our Digital Exchange, we enable the tokenization and digital custody of alternative assets. This end-to-end solution simplifies and expedites the trading of smaller asset blocks, ultimately facilitating access and liquidity in private markets. Innovative Financial Ecosystem: Our journey has seen us transition from securities trading and distribution of comprehensive products, including equities, private credit, funds, and asset-backed securities (“ABS”) (representing Real World Assets ("RWA") like whiskies, wines, art, watches, and real estate) to include fund management and digital custody services.

As the only integrated securities exchange, brokerage, and fund management group with the necessary regulatory licenses and a proven track record in Southeast Asia, we are actively exploring new channels and partnerships to extend our impact to entrepreneurs and investors globally. Established in 2016 and headquartered in Singapore, Alta operates offices globally. We welcome energetic and creative individuals to be part of this ambitious journey with us.
We’re looking for a Chief Financial Officer to build and lead the finance and operations backbone of our new asset management business in Bahrain.

This is a greenfield, founding-team role. Working hand-in-hand with the CEO and Senior Management, you will be responsible for standing up the Bahrain office and establishing the fund — from entity setup, licensing and regulatory approvals through to fund structuring, launch and day-to-day operations. Once live, you will own the financial leadership and operational running of the business as it scales across the region. Beyond finance and operations, this role carries significant governance responsibility. You will work closely with the Board on corporate governance, strategy and oversight matters, and serve as a key member of the Investment Committee. You will also work closely with the risk management team and other middle and back office functions — including compliance, legal, fund administration and operations — to ensure the business runs on sound controls and processes.
The role requires regular travel to Bahrain, extended in-country stays during the setup phase, and openness to potential relocation as the business grows. In practice, this involves:
Partnering with the CEO and Senior Management to design and execute the Bahrain market-entry plan, including timelines, budgets and resourcing
Leading the end-to-end setup of the Bahrain office: legal entity establishment, premises, banking relationships, vendors, IT and infrastructure
Driving the licensing and regulatory approval process with the Central Bank of Bahrain (CBB), working closely with external counsel and compliance advisors
Establishing the fund(s): structuring, domiciliation, documentation, and appointment of fund administrator, custodian, auditor and legal counsel
Building the local operating model — policies, processes, governance frameworks and reporting lines consistent with Group standards
Supporting the Board on corporate governance matters, including board reporting, meeting coordination and governance frameworks
Serving as a key member of the Investment Committee, contributing to investment evaluation, approval and portfolio oversight
Working closely with the risk management team and other middle and back office functions to embed sound controls, processes and escalation paths
Recruiting, onboarding and leading the initial Bahrain team across finance, operations and support functions
Acting as the primary financial and operational interface between the Bahrain entity and Group HQ in Singapore

As this role sits at the intersection of finance, operations, governance and strategy, you’ll need to be comfortable operating without a playbook — applying sound judgement, navigating a new regulatory environment, and knowing when to build, when to delegate and when to escalate. This is as much a builder role as it is a leadership one: you’ll be hands-on in the setup, then grow into leading the function as the team and business scale.
Some Of The Key Responsibilities Include
Own the Bahrain entity's financial strategy, planning, budgeting and forecasting
Build accounting, treasury, tax, audit and reporting functions to CBB standards
Lead end-to-end fund setup: structuring, documentation, service providers, investor readiness
Run fund finance operations: capital calls, distributions, NAV, fees, LP reporting
Ensure smooth integration and consolidated reporting with Group HQ
Serve as the Board's key partner on governance and oversight matters
Establish the governance framework: board structures, charters, delegations, policies
Coordinate Board/committee meetings, board packs, resolutions and minutes
Support strategic decision-making with financial analysis and commercial insight
Manage statutory filings and external auditor/company secretary relationships
Act as a key Investment Committee member, contributing to investment evaluation and monitoring
Provide financial due diligence, valuation input and risk-reward analysis
Work closely with risk management, compliance, legal, fund admin and operations
Ensure sound controls, effective risk reporting, and CBB/AML compliance
Stand up the Bahrain office: entity, premises, banking, insurance, IT, vendors
Support CBB licensing: applications, regulator engagement, post-license conditions
Build the local operating model and recruit the initial Bahrain team
Manage regulator, bank, service provider and government stakeholder relationships
Serve as the senior in-country leader advising the CEO and Board
q: 10+ years of experience in financial services, with significant time in asset management, fund management or investment banking; prior CFO, COO or Head of Finance/Operations experience strongly preferred.
Proven track record setting up a regulated entity, fund or new office from the ground up — ideally in the GCC / MENA region
Strong knowledge of fund structures, fund operations and fund accounting, including administrator, custodian and auditor oversight.
Demonstrated experience supporting Boards and investment committees, with a strong grasp of corporate governance frameworks and practices.
Strong working knowledge of risk management, controls and regulatory risk requirements, with experience partnering closely with risk management, compliance and other middle and back office functions.
Familiarity with CBB regulation, or the ability to ramp up quickly; experience with MAS, FCA or DFSA/FSRA regimes is a plus.
Professional qualification preferred (CPA, CA, ACCA, CFA or equivalent); MBA advantageous.
Strong stakeholder management skills, with confidence engaging Board members, regulators, investors, service providers and internal teams at all levels.
Strong commercial judgement, with the ability to balance business objectives against operational, governance and regulatory considerations.
Highly collaborative, with a track record of partnering effectively across Risk, Legal, Compliance, Product, Technology, Deal and Group finance teams.
Comfortable operating in a fast-paced and evolving environment, with the willingness to remain hands-on while building the function and developing the team.
Experience with Shariah-compliant structures, fintech/digital assets or private markets is a plus.
Willing and able to travel frequently to Bahrain, undertake extended in-country stays, and open to potential relocation.
If you are interested, please send your resume to jobs@alta.exchange!

This team is responsible for generating, executing, and fostering Scale’s work outside of the United States. There are three core types of work involved:
Building custom AI applications for government
Providing high-quality training data for research institutions building LLMs from scratch

5+ years of total work experience, with experience in consulting or as a technical program management role in industry

A proven track record in B2B client facing roles and expanding client relationships

Great cross-functional experience and collaborative ability

d: Our Group Procurement & Logistics team delivers strategic sourcing and integrated supply chain solutions that strengthen operational resilience, optimise value and enable sustainable business performance.

The Manager Supply Chain Operations and Services will lead and manage end-to-end Supply Chain Operations and Group-wide functional governance and performance management of logistics services. They will ensure reliable, compliant and cost-effective distribution center operations, supply continuity, inventory and working-capital efficiency, service performance, compliance and cost effectiveness across planning, replenishment, warehousing, distribution, transportation and trade compliance. The role will drive an integrated operating model through standardised processes, digital enablement, performance governance and continuous improvement, while developing the people and capabilities required to support current and future business needs.
q: Hold an attested Bachelor's Degree or Masters degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Procurement,Operations Management, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration/MBA, or a related discipline.

10+ years of experience in an experience in supply chain, logistics, distribution, warehousing or another complex operational environment, including significant management responsibility in a multi-country or matrix organisation.
A recognised professional qualification in supply chain, logistics, procurement or operations management is preferred. Such as CIPS, CILT, CSCP or equivalent.

Experience should cover several of the following: demand and supply planning, inventory management, distribution centers, international transportation, freight markets, warehousing, customs and trade compliance, strategic third-party logistics providers, outsourced control-tower operations and large-scale transformation.
Aviation or another highly regulated and operationally critical environment is preferred.

r: Lead and manage the Supply Chain Operations and Services function by developing and implementing tactical plans, priorities and objectives for the area of accountability, ensuring delivery of departmental strategy and business objectives. Set performance expectations and oversee multidisciplinary teams covering planning, replenishment, inventory management, distribution centres, logistics, supplier performance and trade compliance to ensure effective operational execution.

Direct end-to-end supply chain execution of Uniform Distribution Centers, the General Distribution Center, warehousing, transportation and associated logistics services , ensuring consistent operating standards, capacity planning, resource deployment, operational readiness, service quality, inventory accuracy and effective fulfilment across all relevant locations and customer channels.

Lead freight, transportation and warehousing services supporting Emirates business requirements, including air, sea and road movements and third-party logistics providers. Optimize capacity, routing, consolidation, service levels and total logistics cost. Monitor freight-market, carrier-capacity, geopolitical and regulatory developments and translate material risks into sourcing input, contingency planning and network decisions.

Maintain accountability for product availability, supply continuity and inventory performance by directing the team to establish robust demand forecasting, appropriate inventory policies, segmentation, safety-stock levels and replenishment parameters, and to control stock-outs, excess, slow-moving and obsolete inventory.

Manage strategic logistics providers and outsourced service arrangements by establishing clear governance, service-level agreements, performance measures, reporting requirements and escalation protocols. Direct provider reviews, corrective actions, mobilisation and operational transitions in collaboration with Procurement and relevant business stakeholders.

Provide leadership and governance for customs and trade-compliance activities, ensuring that responsible teams, customs brokers and logistics providers maintain appropriate controls over declarations, tariff classification, duties and taxes, records, permits and regulatory authorisations.

Lead supply chain transformation and continuous improvement initiatives across warehouse operations, logistics network optimisation, regional distribution centres, systems implementation, process standardisation and new service solutions. Develop business cases, implementation plans and change management activities to support successful delivery, stakeholder adoption and measurable business benefits.
